title: Anticholinergic burden at hospital discharge and injurious falls in adults aged 70 and over: a cohort study using linked pharmacy and admission records
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between anticholinergic burden at discharge and injurious falls within 90 days in adults aged 70 and over. Design: cohort of first eligible discharges from medical wards over two years, using hospital dispensing records linked to regional admission data. Exposure: burden score 3 or more versus 0 to 2. Outcome: first emergency visit or admission for a fall with injury. Analysis: cause-specific Cox model adjusted for frailty, indication and ten other pre-specified covariates. Results and conclusions will be written after the analysis.
introduction: Medicines with anticholinergic effects are common in older adults and are plausibly linked to falls, but recalled studies conflict once frailty is accounted for, and a recorded search for the weeks after hospital discharge returned no records. The answer decides whether routine pharmacist deprescribing review is worth its cost.
methods: Existing dispensing records for discharges between October 2024 and September 2026 are linked to regional admission and emergency records. Frailty is measured from discharge diagnoses with medicine-related codes removed. The primary analysis is a cause-specific Cox model with death as a competing event, with new-user, active-comparator, 30-day window and negative control sensitivity analyses specified in advance.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the cohort flow, exposure distribution, event counts, crude and adjusted hazard ratios with confidence intervals, and the sensitivity and subgroup analyses named in the protocol.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the estimate against the published literature once it has been retrieved and checked, examine whether frailty adjustment explains any difference, and state what the result means for routine deprescribing review.
limitations: Residual confounding by frailty and indication; exposure after discharge uncertain beyond 30 days; falls that do not reach hospital are not captured.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be limited to the association in this population and will not claim that deprescribing prevents falls.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
